The Staff Attorney will report to and work closely with the Director of the Environmental Law Clinic (“Clinic”) and/or other Clinic faculty. Under the direction of the Director of the Clinic or other Clinic faculty, the Staff Attorney will work on all aspects of client representation, including: legal research; drafting memoranda, pleadings, briefs, and other court filings; conducting informal and formal discovery; participating in trials and appeals, and appearing on behalf of Clinic clients. In addition to litigation-related tasks, the Staff Attorney’s nonlitigation responsibilities may include providing clients with legal advice, public speaking and other forms of oral and written advocacy, media appearances, and administrative clinic support such as case intake, planning and managing events, and meeting with stakeholders.

In addition to taking responsibility for their own case load and working independently on Clinic matters (including when students are between semesters, on break, or unavailable), the Staff Attorney will work collaboratively and closely with Clinic students on Clinic matters. That can include working in parallel with students, and providing guidance, suggestions, and direction as Clinic students develop their skills while representing clients.

This is an ideal position for those seeking to gain experience and training before pursuing a career in a public interest environmental law practice and, while not a fellowship or instructor position, the position may also provide useful training and experience for those interested in pursuing a career in clinical teaching.
The expected pay range for this recruitment is $65,700- $100,000 (Annual).
This position is being recruited at a variable 50% to 100% FTE.
Member in good standing of the State Bar of California and maintain that standing through continuing legal education credits required by the State Bar
Career intention to practice in public interest, public sector, and/or clinical setting.
Alternatively a member of the Bar of another State who meets the requirements of, and successfully registers as, a legal aid attorney under California Rule of Court 9.45.
Excellent communication, writing, and editing skills, with demonstrated ability to be detail oriented
Excellent time management skills, and the ability to manage diverse activities and meet critical deadlines with minimal supervision.

Solid knowledge of legal research computer applications, document sharing technology and research tools.
